solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feature of endgame employing belt- and-braces tactic?

definitions.meaning: in chess, a move giving check with two pieces at once, a late-game resource
verifying something twice over, a doubly cautious approach like wearing both belt and braces

explanation.surface: A cautious chess player's plan for the closing stage of a game, wearing both belt and braces.
explanation.walkthrough: Belt-and-braces is British for taking two precautions where one would do; braces are what Americans call suspenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess check delivered by two pieces at once, and also the everyday habit of verifying twice for safety.

clue.text: Expression of respect and honour that's peripheral to South African party

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits around the outside of what follows, so it is placed on its periphery

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for South
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: A tribute paid with honour that stays on the margins of a South African political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peripheral to' puts I and E around SANC, giving ISANCE after OBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of deference such as a bow, so it expresses respect.

clue.text: Beautiful Italian girl, one of two employed in plant producing drug

indicators.note: the plant's name is two Italian words joined, and only the first of the pair is wanted, the other dropped

parts.note: belladonna, deadly nightshade, is the source of the drug atropine

explanation.surface: A lovely Italian girl working at a pharmaceutical plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Belladonna is Italian 'bella donna', beautiful lady; take just one of those two words. 'Plant' looks industrial but is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Bella is Italian for beautiful and also a girl's given name, so it fits a lovely Italian girl.

clue.text: Perhaps "smiley" and "laughing" feelings must conceal dejection at heart?

indicators.note: the feelings word holds the next letter inside it, concealing it
the very centre letter of the word dejection is picked out

explanation.surface: Wondering whether cheerful and laughing feelings hide a core of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' gives C, the centre of 'dejection', which 'must conceal' places within EMOTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Smiley and laughing faces are examples of the little symbols people type to show mood in messages.

clue.text: Complaint misses point from the outset, and it's pivotal

indicators.note: the complaint goes without one letter, missing it
the dropped letter comes from the very start of the word

parts.note: a whinge is a British word for a moan or complaint
W, West, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A grumble that drops its point at once, yet is still central to the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' and 'from the outset' remove the opening W, a compass point, from WHINGE, British slang for a moan.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the joint on which a door or lid pivots, so it is literally pivotal.

clue.text: Form of piracy holding everyone up in vessel

indicators.note: the rearranged letters grip the next piece inside them
a new form of the word piracy means rearranging its letters
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A type of piracy that holds everybody up aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word for everyone because this is a down clue. 'Vessel' suggests a ship but is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: A capillary is one of the tiny blood vessels linking arteries to veins.

clue.text: Understated chic in Galliano cap or coat

indicators.note: the letters lie quietly within the phrase, not openly stated

explanation.surface: A designer's subtle chic, as seen in a Galliano hat or coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understated' signals a run of letters inside 'chic in Galliano'. John Galliano is a fashion designer, but 'cap or coat' is about cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar frosting tops or covers a cake, so it caps or coats it.

clue.text: Old king looks tense and extremely pale

parts.note: eyes as a verb, looks at
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An ageing monarch eyes something tense and looks very pallid.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a dull, colourless shade, so the most washed-out or wan.

clue.text: Trump's worthless talk-show discontented with final notice

indicators.note: with its contents taken out, only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: an obit, obituary, is the last notice of a life in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A jibe that a president's chat show is rubbish and lacking content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' leaves TW, the outsides of 'talk-show'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two bits was a quarter dollar, so a two-bit thing is cheap and of little value.

clue.text: Turner: he exhibited in west and east London at first

indicators.note: the word he is shown placed inside the pair that follows

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west
E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the city is used

explanation.surface: J. M. W. Turner the painter showing work in galleries across London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter but means anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel is something that rotates, a turning device.

clue.text: No hope, unfortunately, on French island for one who likes a drink

indicators.note: the letters of no hope fall out badly, arranged in an unlucky new order

explanation.surface: A hopeless drinker marooned on an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a lover and connoisseur of wine.

clue.text: Am I bats to stew this?

definitions.text: Am I bats to stew this?

indicators.note: stewing churns things up, so these letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook wonders if they are crazy to stew this grain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue asks whether it is mad to stew this rice, which is normally boiled or steamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a long-grain aromatic rice, which one would hardly stew.

clue.text: Poem in London's District Line magazine missing verse?

parts.note: EC is the postal district of East Central London

indicators.note: the magazine name lacks one letter here

explanation.surface: A poem found in a magazine for a London Underground line, but without any verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The District Line is a London Underground route, but the words split as 'London's District' (EC) and 'Line' (L).
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, often a dialogue between shepherds.

clue.text: Made adjustment, having changed course without resistance

indicators.note: the word goes with one letter left out

parts.note: turned, as a ship changing direction
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Someone adjusted, steering a new course without any resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument or engine that has been tuned has been finely adjusted.

clue.text: Heated dry vigorously to .….?

indicators.note: the letters are shaken up vigorously into a new order

explanation.surface: Drying something hard with heat until it is... dried out, with the dots standing for the result.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots leave the result to be filled in: heating something dry vigorously does this to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove all the water from something, as heating hard would.

clue.text: Attack batting side by sledging — when Border's gone, by anything

parts.note: the on side is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: once the border has gone, only what remains of the word sledging counts

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: Cricket: an attack on the batting side by sledging after Allan Border, the Australian captain, has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Sledging is verbal abuse of a batsman in cricket; Allan Border was an Australian captain. 'when Border's gone' removes EDGING, leaving SL.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, sustained assault.

clue.text: Filthy place to file originals of iconic collection of fashion

parts.note: a pigsty, a sty, is a byword for a filthy place
a file is a list, a row

indicators.note: originals are the first letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A grubby place for filing the original pieces of a classic fashion collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylistic means relating to style, which is fashion in dress or design.

clue.text: Old person rolling cigar tries to give up smoking? Hardly at all!

indicators.note: rolling a cigar mixes up its letters into a new order
giving up means the following letter is let go
only a scrap of the word smoking, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: An elderly smoker rolling a cigar tries to quit smoking, but scarcely manages it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly at all' takes only a token scrap of 'smoking', and 'to give up' drops that from 'tries' before 'rolling' mixes everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric describes the elderly, and is used informally as a noun for an aged person.

clue.text: Impetuous doctor shaves Tory without soap to begin with

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order
one letter is left out of the word
only the first letter of the word soap is meant

explanation.surface: A rash doctor shaves a Conservative without even soaping first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' and 'to begin with' drop S, the first of 'soap', from SHAVES; 'doctor' then rearranges HAVES and TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhasty means acting too quickly and rashly, as impetuous people do.

clue.text: Interminable road examination soaks up money

indicators.note: the exam word absorbs the next piece inside it

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bit is a small coin, money

explanation.surface: An endless road test that drains your money.
explanation.walkthrough: A British orbital is a ring road around a city, endless because it loops back on itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road circling a city never ends, so it is a road without termination.

clue.text: Express reverses across road a short way?

indicators.note: the turned word spans across the next piece, holding it inside
the word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: An express train backs over a road for a little distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses' turns SAY to YAS, which goes 'across' RD.
explanation.definitionFit: A few yards is a short distance, so the plural unit stands for a short way.

clue.text: Expert supporting the Spanish revolutionary provides comfort

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting piece goes underneath, after the other
a revolutionary turns over, so the word is turned backwards

explanation.surface: An expert backing a Spanish rebel offers comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' means the expert sits beneath, so comes last; 'revolutionary' turns the Spanish article round.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation in distress, a form of comfort.

clue.text: Second-class teams must retain energy — or else!

indicators.note: the team words hold the next letter inside them

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A warning that reserve teams must keep their energy, or else.
explanation.walkthrough: B sides are second teams; 'must retain' puts E between B and SIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides means in addition, otherwise, much as 'else' adds something further.

clue.text: Something fundamental about types giving rise to passions

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A basic truth about personality types that stirs strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fundamental' suggests basic, but means at the foot of a letter in printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is a small stroke at the base of letters in some typefaces, part of the type.

clue.text: Recycling instruments could be accidental

indicators.note: a letter is cycled from one end of the word to the other

explanation.surface: Musical instruments thrown in recycling might end up there by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycling' moves the end S of HARPS to the front. 'accidental' is the musical term, not chance.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an accidental is a sign raising or lowering a note, a sharp being one such.

clue.text: Institution completely put in place

parts.note: all, as in all done, means completely

explanation.surface: An institution is fully set up and in position.
explanation.definitionFit: To install is to set equipment or a person in position.

clue.text: Dance like girl endlessly twirling

indicators.note: twirling turns round, so the pieces are read backwards
the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A dance like that of a girl spinning on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts LASS to LAS; 'twirling' turns ASLAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Administered severe criticism to cut down culture

parts.note: to reap is to cut down a crop

explanation.surface: A critic laid into something, slashing at the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearing something apart is attacking it harshly in words, savaging it.

clue.text: A third of licensees covered your song

indicators.note: the three letters wrap around the next piece
the opening third of the nine-letter word licensees, three letters

explanation.surface: Some pub licensees cover a song of yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A third of' takes the first three of the nine letters of 'licensees'; 'covered' wraps them round the abbreviation of 'your'. Licensees in Britain run pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrics are the words of a song, and a lyric is also a short song-like poem.

clue.text: Hope sentence begins with a temporal indication

indicators.note: the sentence word comes at the start, before the hope word

explanation.surface: Hope that a prison sentence starts with an indication of time.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the expected length of time a person will live, an estimate of years.
